build_note: Update this file with every release.

features.name: Editor shell and Motion kit look
features.what: Top bar, panels, status island, keycaps, springs: the kit ported to egui.

features.name: Editor and Builder movement
features.what: Caps Lock switches; orbit, pan, proximity zoom; fly with 12 speeds; F frames the selection.

features.name: Projects, save, undo and file drop
features.what: Project folders of plain text; save / open / new; undo and redo; unsaved-changes question; Assets panel with dropped files.

features.name: Basic shapes, placing and the move widget
features.what: Box, ramp, stairs, arch, cylinder, sphere, plane; drop on surfaces; move and turn with snapping; shapes double as colliders.

features.name: Scene list
features.what: Find, select and hide parts by name.

features.name: glTF model import
features.what: Drop .glb / .gltf files and place them like shapes; they collide too.

features.name: Test mode with the walker
features.what: ` plays from the reticle, Shift+` from the Player start; a plain walker until characters exist.

features.name: Windows game export
features.what: File > Export Windows game zips the game player with the project.

features.name: Wires, buttons and moving parts
features.what: Interact buttons, Moves on any shape (Go / Back / Toggle), wires picked in the properties panel, the walker rides moving parts.

features.name: Help menu, About and updates
features.what: About Beverly and Check for updates (download, check, swap; runs from the next start).

features.name: Features window
features.what: Help > Features: what's planned, built and next, updated with every release.

features.name: Scripted tests
features.what: Tests that load a level, press keys or actions on a timeline, save screenshots and check positions, on a fixed clock so the same script always gives the same result; they work with a game's own character too.
features.note: Pushed forward by the user (2026-11-15). Also records Last Ascent's mech as it plays today (positions per step for scripted runs), so its port to a character file can be checked against the real thing. Bevy's manual time step keeps runs repeatable.

features.name: Settings panels from data
features.what: Every building block's settings panel is generated from its data: word sliders with numbers under More, toggles, colours, lists, in the Motion kit style; key panels get custom designs later.
features.note: Built on bevy_reflect: each setting is an attribute on its field (label, kind, section, unit, help; word sliders with their words and end values). One description serves the panel, the MCP server (settings::describe), and later saving, the timeline's keyable values and the network. Range ends changed under More are kept in the file they belong to. The part panel is the first one drawn this way.

features.name: Scale handles
features.what: Corner cubes scale the whole part (the opposite corner stays), face cubes stretch it along one axis; Shift scales from the middle, Ctrl turns snapping off; type a number during any drag (move, turn, scale) and Enter sets it exactly, Esc cancels.
features.note: Asked for by the user (2026-11-15), so built ahead of its place in the order.

features.name: MCP server
features.what: A local server (off by default) that lets an AI assistant such as Claude Code read the project, place and change parts, look through the camera, play the level and run tests, every change undoable like your own.
chunks: The server, ported from Prism 3D's (both protocol versions, a token, this computer only, Help > MCP Server with the switch, token, copy-ready command and recent calls); every menu item and shortcut becomes a named editor action; read the project, levels, parts, selection, wires, assets and the log; run actions

Editing and seeing: place, change and delete parts with any of their settings (tools built from the same setting descriptions as the panels, so new building blocks need no new tools), wires; screenshots from the current view or any camera; move the editor camera
Playing and testing: start and stop test mode, press keys, read the player and parts while playing; scripted tests, bakes and builds run as jobs to check on, so long work doesn't time out
features.note: Built 2026-11-15 in three parts: the server (Prism's protocol half reused: both versions, token, local only), Help > MCP Server, the named actions the menus and keys use too; reading, editing (tools built from the setting descriptions, so new building blocks need no new tools), wires, screenshots and the view; play-testing and background jobs for scripted tests and exports. Check: tests/mcp/check.py. Editor only: never in an exported game. Every later feature's brief says what it adds here.

features.name: The .bev file extension
features.what: project.bev, levels/*.bev, characters/*.bev, each with a format version so files from older Beverlys are upgraded when opened; old .ron projects still open.
features.note: Files are RON text with a format number first (FORMAT in level.rs); saving an old project writes .bev in place of its .ron files. The editor and player also take a .bev file's path (Explorer's Open with). Test projects: tests/lift (.bev) and tests/old-ron-project (.ron), same trace. MCP: nothing new needed; its tools work on the open project in either format.

features.name: Instancing and Unique
features.what: Mesh-plus-material parts are drawn as instances; changing one asks “change all, or make this one unique?”
features.note: Bevy already draws identical mesh-plus-material pairs in batches, so this is mostly the editor side: shared assets, Unique, and keeping models sharing one mesh.

features.name: Textures and materials
features.what: Drop a texture on a face or a whole shape, texture handles, reusable materials in Assets.
chunks: Textures on parts and faces: drop, scale, offset, the violet texture handles
Material assets shared by many surfaces, the Materials panel, glowing-surface material

features.name: Lights, sun and sky
features.what: Point and spot light parts with handles; the sun; Interior mode; a light budget meter.
chunks: Point and spot light parts with radius and cone handles, shadows on or off
Sun light with direction and shadows, Interior mode (no sun), light budget meter
features.note: The sky and the time-of-day slider are in Sky and clouds; the running clock in Day and night.

features.name: Surface tags
features.what: Mark parts climbable, diggable, water, grind rail, perch spot, slippery.

features.name: Camera parts
features.what: Fixed, Rail, Orbit and Follow cameras with frustum pyramids; Look through; Camera focus and Release actions.
chunks: Fixed / Orbit / Follow camera parts, frustums, Look through
Rail cameras on paths, Camera focus / Release actions with ease
features.note: Rail cameras need Paths.

features.name: Physics for loose objects
features.what: Avian becomes the one collision world: level parts and models get colliders, moving parts are kinematic, crates and barrels tumble, characters push and stand on them, blasts shove them.
chunks: Avian as the only collision world: colliders for shapes and models (box, hull, convex pieces, exact for still things), still / moving / loose parts, a fixed time step with smoothing; Moves become moving bodies; the old collision code retires
The walker on bevy_tnua (slopes, steps, moving platforms); a game's own character (Last Ascent's mech) asks Avian instead of its own copy of the meshes
Loose parts: mass, friction, sleeping; characters push and stand on them; impulses from blasts and the winch
features.note: Two collision worlds side by side (today's and Avian's) would need every moving part kept in step twice, so Avian replaces today's. Loose things need convex shapes (Avian builds them from the mesh: collider-from-mesh); exact mesh colliders only for things that never move. avian3d 0.8 supports Bevy 0.20 and has f64 and enhanced-determinism options for big worlds and multiplayer.

features.name: Navigation areas
features.what: One button builds where enemies can walk; patrol paths.
features.note: vleue_navigator supports Bevy 0.20.

features.name: World settings
features.what: Per level: ground (none, flat floor, terrain, ocean), sky or Interior. Space games get no ground at all.

features.name: Zone parts
features.what: One stretchable Zone part with settings for weather, post-processing, audio, wind, water, boundaries and hazards, blending at its edges.

features.name: Particle effects
features.what: One particle system for every effect: bursts and streams of soft blobs with drag, gravity, spin and wander, size and colour over life drawn as curves.
features.note: Generalises Last Ascent's particles (fx.rs and the plume particles), which already match the game's look and run without compute shaders. bevy_hanabi (GPU, Bevy 0.20) stays a fallback if counts outgrow it. Rain and snow are a shader around the camera, not particles.

features.name: Sound parts and audio zones
features.what: Sound parts, the Sound action, ambient loops, music regions, reverb in zones, and sounds on everything: characters, weather, parts and effects play sounds when things happen.
chunks: Sound parts and the Sound action, 3D sound, volume and range
Audio settings on Zone parts: ambience, music regions, reverb
Sound hooks: any event (a footstep, a move, a hit, a wire firing) plays a sound; footsteps by surface; a Sounds list on characters and on zones that later features (weather, effects, idles) add to
features.note: Gets its own planning pass before building (user, 2026-11-15: adding sounds to characters, sets and weather needs attention). bevy_kira_audio supports Bevy 0.20.

features.name: Prism models: named pieces
features.what: Groups from Prism arrive as named pieces; components as shared instances (with Prism's export brief).

features.name: Jump pads
features.what: Step on it and get launched in its direction; works on enemies and objects.

features.name: Character files and the Characters tab
features.what: characters/*.bev, the Characters tab: list, preview, character sheet and cards; the walker becomes the first character file.
chunks: Character file and loader; the player is spawned from it; the walker becomes characters/humanoid.bev
Characters tab: list, live preview, character sheet with cards that open when relevant, card pages
Create steps: template, model, fit (auto collision); Body card
features.note: Undo covers character files the same way it covers levels (each open file keeps its own undo).

features.name: Ocean
features.what: Waves from a formula (layered Gerstner), shore fade, foam; settings by wind and storm.
features.note: bevy_water supports Bevy 0.20.

features.name: Post-processing
features.what: Per level or camera: bloom, depth of field, motion blur, chromatic aberration, vignette, lens distortion, auto exposure, colour grading; zones and the timeline can change them.
features.note: All built into Bevy 0.20.

features.name: Ambient occlusion, reflections and fog volumes
features.what: Screen-space ambient occlusion and reflections, volumetric fog and light shafts, quality settings.
features.note: All built into Bevy 0.20.

features.name: Sky and clouds
features.what: Physical atmosphere with time of day, sun and moon, stars; cloud layers that drift with the wind.
chunks: Atmosphere sky, sun and moon, stars, time of day
Cloud layers and volumetric clouds that follow the wind
features.note: Bevy 0.20 has a physical atmosphere built in.

features.name: Wind
features.what: One wind for the level (direction, strength, gusts, zones) read by foliage, cloth, flags, particles, smoke, sails and flying lift.

features.name: Decals
features.what: Scorch marks, cracks, skid grooves, bullet holes and signs projected onto surfaces, fading with age.
features.note: Bevy 0.20 has decals built in. Blast, crack and scrape marks are drawn by a shader from a few numbers (Last Ascent's are small images today; the no-raster rule asks for math where it can do the job); signs and graffiti use the user's own images.

features.name: Test snapshot and keep changes
features.what: Leaving test mode puts back everything that moved, broke or was used up; values tuned while testing are offered to keep.
features.note: Needed as soon as loose physics parts exist, so it comes right after physics instead of at the end.

features.name: Generated sounds
features.what: Temporary sounds made from a few settings: blips, hits, footsteps, whooshes, explosions, engine hums and rain, saved as their settings (tiny) and swapped for real recordings whenever you have them.
features.note: User, 2026-11-15: generated temporary sounds are fine. Works like the classic sfxr sound makers: a wave, a pitch slide, an envelope and noise.

features.name: Haze, weather and zones
features.what: Haze, rain / snow / ash / embers; Zone parts that override them; Set weather action over time.
chunks: Level atmosphere: haze colour and density, precipitation (rain, snow, ash, embers) blown by the wind
Atmosphere settings on Zone parts (Interior preset); Set weather action over time
features.note: Haze is Bevy's distance fog; local fog banks are fog volumes (ambient occlusion and fog volumes feature). Rain and wind sounds go through the sound hooks.

features.name: Several levels and level exits
features.what: More than one level per project; Level exit parts wired to the next level.

features.name: Variables
features.what: Flags and counters such as “has key” or “enemies left”, readable by wires and the HUD.

features.name: The shared timeline
features.what: One timeline widget for sequences, animatics, light FX, weather, spawn waves and menus.
chunks: Timeline panel: ruler, transport, playhead, scrubbing the level live
Tracks, clips, keys and markers: add, drag, trim, Alt-copy; markers fire wires
Sequence part: the timeline as a part with Play / Stop / Jump to and an output per marker; list view
Curve lane and easing; clips that are timelines (dive in, breadcrumb)
Distance ruler for rails and moving platforms; Moves upgraded to keys on the timeline

features.name: Ways of moving and switching rules

chunks: Mode machine: walk & run, fall, jump with feel settings, coyote time, jump buffer
Rules editor and the library picker (+ Add) with needs; editable ranges
features.note: bevy_tnua (Bevy 0.20) does walking, jumping with coyote time, crouching and dashing on Avian; the + Add library picker is shared with parts, abilities, effects and items.

features.name: Character camera and controls
features.what: Third / first person rig, distance, shake per event; actions mapped to keys, rebinding.

features.name: Joint chains and procedural animation

Auto-detect chains from the model's shape; click-to-fix on the model
Joint tree by name: drag joints between chains, rename

features.name: Attributes, effects and abilities
features.what: Values like health, fuel, heat and ammo; effects that change them; abilities with costs and cooldowns; events that trigger cues.
chunks: Attributes and effects (instant and over time), events
Abilities with costs and cooldowns; the Abilities card with its tags

features.name: Art styles
features.what: Cel shading in 2–5 bands, outlines (cheap shell outlines or precise edge detection), painterly and flat looks; a per-project look.
chunks: Toon material with bands and ramp, rim light
Outlines: shell per object and edge detection over the screen; per-project style presets
features.note: bevy_mod_outline supports Bevy 0.20.

features.name: Polish pass: friction and looks

chunks: Friction hunt: build a real level start to finish (with a scripted run and screenshots), list every extra click, unclear word, missing keycap or slow path, and fix the worst
Looks: spacing, alignment, type sizes, colours, springs and entrances across every window built so far; one style for empty states, hints and errors
Check: before-and-after screenshots of every window at full size and in a small window, kept with the test projects
features.note: Placed after step 6 of the Last Ascent path on purpose (not by its needs): by then the editor has most of its panels. MCP: nothing new to add; the before-and-after screenshots are taken through the server's screenshot tool.

features.name: Automatic LOD and draw distance

chunks: Auto-LOD on import with cross-fades, LOD rings on the ground, Colour by LOD
Draw-distance classes tied to the haze end, Always visible flag

chunks: Paths tool: click points, bend handles, closed loops; paths as level parts
Animating overlay (P): keys and handles in the world, ticks for timing, fly-to-record
features.note: One path system for rails, patrols, rivers, roads, terrain curves, camera paths and boundaries.

features.name: Save points and saved games
features.what: Save point parts store the player, variables and which parts fired; load from the menu.
features.note: Everything a save needs (moving parts mid-move, fired wires, variables) lives in data, the same rule multiplayer needs.

features.name: Animation clips and blending

chunks: Clip playback and blending by speed; one clip slot per mode
Pose and key: animate a character made of separate pieces (Prism's named groups) by turning its joints on the timeline, saved as clips
Transitions per move, animation events (footsteps, effects), layering with joint jobs
features.note: Skinned characters bring their clips in the GLB (the user will skin in another tool, Prism once it can). Characters made of separate pieces, like the mech, are posed and keyed here, since Prism exports pieces with pivots.

features.name: Jump family

chunks: Ledge detection; mantle; ledge grab and shimmy
Wall-run and wall-cling with their exits into jumps

Manoeuvres as moves: rolls, dive, loop, Immelmann / split-S, stall, boost

features.name: Swimming and diving

features.name: Health, shields and death

notes.title: Idles, barks and interaction
notes.text: Crowds look wrong when everyone plays the same idle: guides suggest 3–5 idle variations per character type and random offsets so footsteps don't sync. Fidgets (scratching, looking around) start after standing still a while. Head look-at is a cheap procedural layer, and hands reach handles with two-bone IK that blends in and out; holding is easy, the blend is the hard part.

notes.title: Driving
notes.text: Arcade handling starts simple and adds mechanics until it feels right: steering limited by speed (curbs understeer), the handbrake locks the rear wheels to start a drift, clean drifts refill boost, boost is spent on the way out. Simulation adds weight transfer and counter-steering; Beverly's vehicles start arcade with those as settings.
sources: Racing game approaches and trade-offs (Game Developer)
Need for Speed Heat handling model (EA)

notes.title: Flying
notes.text: Arcade flight keeps pitch, yaw and roll with automatic banking in turns, plus speed and lift limits. Manoeuvres become moves: aileron roll (a full roll), barrel roll (a roll with a pull, evasive), dive, loop, Immelmann (half loop and half roll: turn back, gain height), split-S (the reverse: turn back, gain speed), stall turn, boost.
sources: How to barrel roll (World of Warplanes)

notes.title: Moves and abilities
notes.text: Platformers hide forgiveness in jumping: coyote time (jump just after leaving an edge) and jump buffering. Air dashes usually reset on landing. Dodges pair a short invulnerability with a step; parries are timed blocks. Shooters add slide, wall-run and mantle; stealth adds crouch tiers, lean, cover and hiding in shadow.

notes.title: World sizes, terrain, caves
notes.text: Positions are 32-bit, so worlds past about 10 km jitter; the fix is a floating origin or camera-relative maths. Heightfields can't make overhangs; games add caves with sculpted volumes (smooth add / subtract shapes turned into meshes) or hand-made pieces, and build dungeons from modular kits, often laid out by a generator. Rooms joined by portals hide what can't be seen indoors; they don't suit open ground. Beverly's terrain is described by curves and strokes, not height images.
sources: Godot: double precision for large worlds

notes.title: Water
notes.text: Oceans layer a few Gerstner waves: stable and easy to tune. Rivers are paths with width, depth and flow speed per point; foam drifts with the flow. Waterfalls are usually custom pieces with mist and ripple rings where they land. Buoyancy samples the water height and pushes things up with drag. In Unreal, water fought with world streaming, so Beverly's water belongs to streaming regions from the start.

notes.title: Look: post-processing, styles, wind
notes.text: Bevy 0.20 already has depth of field, motion blur, bloom, chromatic aberration, vignette, lens distortion, colour grading, auto exposure, SSAO, screen-space reflections, volumetric fog, a physical sky, TAA / SMAA and GPU occlusion culling, so these are mostly editor work. Cel shading bands light into 2–5 steps; outlines are cheap shells (gaps on hard edges) or precise screen edge detection (costlier, noisier); games often mix them. One wind (direction, strength, gusts) feeds foliage sway in two layers, cloth, flags, particles and sails.
sources: Vegetation that reacts to the environment

notes.title: Multiplayer
notes.text: Shooters and most online games use an authoritative server: each player's own moves show at once and are corrected when the server answers. Rollback (every machine simulates and rewinds on a wrong guess) suits two-player fighting games and needs a deterministic game. Multiplayer touches characters, physics, scripting and saving, so if it's wanted it should be decided early, even if it's built late.

notes.title: Space and level edges
notes.text: Classic space games fly like aircraft; Newtonian flight keeps momentum, and Elite layers a switchable flight assist over it so ships stay controllable. For the edge of a level, games warn and count down (“return to the combat area”), push the player back, damage them in a hazard zone or wrap them around; developers report wrapping rarely feels good in 3D and round areas beat square ones.

notes.title: Risks found in the second pass
notes.text: Bevy releases every 3–4 months and each library has to catch up before Beverly can move, so Beverly stays pinned and upgrades on purpose (about a session each time). Physics: one collision world, not two. Animation: Prism has no skeletons yet, so pose and key comes to Beverly. Multiplayer: a fixed time step from the start. Effects: one particle system, Last Ascent's, and the Plume Editor's files as the effect format. Rasters: decals, reflections, foliage and terrain paint are kept as math, strokes or captured at load.
